layman_headline: Market is running hot after a massive rally — patience is the smart play right now.
layman_explanation: Bitcoin just surged nearly 23% in a week and most altcoins are up 20-60%. The market mood is 'Greed' at 74, meaning most people are already bought in and feeling confident. Our existing XRP position is down about 5% after a huge 47% weekly run — it's pulling back which is normal. The swing trade candidates are either overbought (RSI above 74-86) or stablecoins with no trade opportunity. Chasing into extended moves is how swing traders get burned.
layman_action: Hold the current XRP position and let it work toward its target. Don't chase anything new right now — wait for a pullback or a fresh setup with better risk/reward.
expert_reasoning: All actionable swing candidates (LIT RSI 74.6, PUMP RSI 86.1, MON +38.5% 7d, XRP +47.6% 7d) are deeply overbought or massively extended. The composite signal scores are unanimously negative across the board. Bitcoin dominance at 59.2% signals capital is concentrated in BTC rather than flowing freely into alts, making altcoin entries riskier. The Fear & Greed index at 74 with an improving trend suggests we haven't peaked yet, but entering after 20-50% weekly moves violates core swing trading discipline. Our XRP position at -5.1% is still well above its $1.30 stop-loss and the thesis remains intact — the pullback from $1.56 after a 47.6% weekly surge is healthy consolidation.
risk_factors: XRP could continue pulling back if BTC loses $79K support after its parabolic weekly move
High BTC dominance (59.2%) may suppress altcoin recovery, keeping XRP range-bound
Greed sentiment at 74 suggests a broader market correction could materialize quickly
watch_list: BTC price action around $79K-80K — a break below $77K would signal broader risk-off
XRP holding above $1.40 support level — if it breaks, reassess stop-loss positioning
SOL pullback to $90-93 range which would create a favorable swing entry with defined risk
market_context: The market is in a strong greed-driven rally with BTC up 23% weekly and massive ETF inflows of $2.2B in 6 days. However, most assets are now extended and overbought, making new entries high-risk with poor reward-to-risk ratios.
context_banner: Post-rally consolidation phase — discipline means waiting for pullbacks rather than chasing green candles.

key_signals.description: LIT at 74.6 and PUMP at 86.1 RSI — both deep in overbought territory, signaling elevated correction risk and poor entry timing.
Bitcoin ETF inflow streak of $2.2B in 6 days confirms strong institutional demand driving the rally, but this is already priced into the 23% weekly BTC move.
Greed at 74 and improving — market hasn't peaked but entering extended positions at this sentiment level historically yields mixed results (56% win rate in our data).
XRP volume at $5B and ZEC at $1.17B show the rally has been volume-confirmed, but these massive volumes after 47-60% weekly moves suggest climactic buying rather than early accumulation.
Bitcoin slipping from $80K as gold cools suggests the initial momentum burst may be fading, supporting a wait-for-pullback approach.
